load_context.definition: BC Hydro Balancing Authority (BCHA) gross telemetered Control Area Load: hourly average MW for the BC Hydro balancing authority area, which covers British Columbia's interconnected grid. Generation is derived as load + net exports on the BC-US and BC-AB tie lines (the BA's interchange), so load = generation + net imports holds by construction.

statcan_check.note: Derived generation (BCHA load + net tie exports) vs Statistics Canada table 25-10-0015-01, BC total generation, all producers. StatCan also counts generation outside the telemetered BA load (e.g. off-grid and some industrial self-generation), so derived is expected to be a few % lower.

load_context.instantaneous: Not published: BC Hydro has no public 5-minute or instantaneous load/generation feed (the 5-minute real-time page has tie-line flows only), so peaks here are highest hourly averages.

williston.name: Williston
williston.note: Licence live range 642.04–672.08 m (32 MAF). The Peace Water Use Plan often uses a higher normal minimum of 654.41 m.

typical.note: ECCC real-time and HYDAT LEVEL for 07EF003 use an assumed gauge datum, not geodetic elevation. Offset 630.065 m was calibrated on 2026-11-20: BC Hydro wsc.txt reported 668.859 m at 16:20 LST (America/Vancouver) while api.weather.gc.ca hydrometric-realtime LEVEL was 38.794 m at the same instant. Do not use the raw ECCC LEVEL as a pool elevation. The offset is assumed constant across the HYDAT record; if the datum was shifted in some years the medians could be off.

dinosaur.name: Dinosaur

sitec.name: Site C

mica.name: Mica

arrow.name: Arrow

duncan.name: Duncan
duncan.note: Storage only: no generators. Energy is realized downstream on the Kootenay.

kootenay.name: Kootenay Lake
kootenay.note: Natural lake regulated by Corra Linn (FortisBC) under the IJC 1938 Order of Approval. Percent is of the 6-ft IJC band (1739.32–1745.32 ft at Queens Bay). The dashed mark is the Order maximum for this date, not a historical median. No stored-energy figure: the lake is not a simple plant head-pond.

typical.source: IJC 1938 Order of Approval rule curve

reservoirs.total_gwh_note: Sum of local stored-energy estimates for projects with a head assumption (Williston, Dinosaur, Site C, Mica, Arrow). Duncan is excluded.

res_mica.label: Mica / Kinbasket (Corps CWMS, confirmed by BC Hydro grt.txt)

kootenay_fortis.forecast: Nov 25, 2026: Kootenay Lake is forecast to increase to 1744.70 at Queens Bay by December 3, 2026.

assumptions.energy: E ≈ ρ g h V η / 3.6e12 GWh, η = 0.88. Williston and Mica use the mid-elevation of the water now in live storage (constant assumed tailwater). Site C uses an assumed 52 m rated head; Arrow uses an assumed 22 m head. Duncan has no generators. Kootenay Lake has no stored-energy figure (a natural lake; generation is at Corra Linn and the downstream plants). These are engineering estimates, not a dispatch model.
assumptions.percent: Percent full is live storage as a share of the official usable range. Peace projects are linear in elevation (no public Williston storage curve). Mica uses official USACE elevation–storage points (2,320 / 2,434 / 2,475 ft). Linear-in-elevation % is slightly conservative when a reservoir is high (real area is larger at the top). Kootenay Lake percent is of the 6-ft IJC 1938 Order band (1739.32–1745.32 ft at Queens Bay); 1739.32 is a seasonal *maximum* target after 31 March, not a physical empty, so the lake can read slightly below 0% in late winter and well above 100% in freshet.
assumptions.williston_range: Licensed live range 642.04–672.08 m, 32 MAF (Final Water Licence). pct_wup is the same elevation against the tighter Water Use Plan normal floor of 654.41 m.
assumptions.typical: The dashed 'typical for this date' mark on Williston is the median of historical 07EF003 daily means for that month-day, plus the documented 630.065 m geodetic offset in docs/williston_doy_median.json. On Kootenay Lake the dashed mark is the IJC 1938 Order maximum for that date (1745.32 ft from 1 Sep–7 Jan, drawing down to 1739.32 ft by 31 Mar; after 31 Mar the default max is 1739.32 ft and a calculated freshet limit is not modelled). Other reservoirs have no dashed mark yet.
assumptions.coverage: This is the Peace cascade (Williston, Dinosaur, Site C), the Columbia River Treaty projects in BC (Mica, Arrow, Duncan), and IJC-regulated Kootenay Lake (Corra Linn, FortisBC). It is not the whole BC Hydro system: Bridge-Coastal, Campbell River, Stave and other Lower Mainland and Island plants are omitted.
assumptions.kootenay: Level is WSC 08NH064 Kootenay Lake at Queens Bay, geodetic (GSC Datum 1928 Adjustment), via the ECCC / wateroffice APIs. This is the IJC reference gauge and matches FortisBC's Queen's Bay reading. 08NJ158 is 'Kootenay Lake Outflow near Corra Linn' (assumed datum, not realtime) and is not used. FortisBC also publishes a Nelson reading on secure.fortisbc.com/lakelevel/lakes.jsp (scraped as a supplement only). CWMS CORB is Corra Linn forebay, which is not the same as Queens Bay lake level and returned no points in a test pull. No stored-energy estimate is published for the lake.

similar_days.note: Shows correlation, not intent: BC Hydro's reasons for calling an event aren't published, and conditions can differ in ways not measured here (forecasts at notice time, outages, reservoir levels, US prices by hour).

peak_events.baseline_method: Average of the same BC clock hours on the previous 10 weekdays (Mon-Fri) that were not BC statutory holidays and not event days (weekend/holiday events: previous 4 weekend days/holidays). A baseline day counts for a measure only if it has every window hour for that measure; the number of days used is shown. Baseline max load = average of each day's highest window hour.
notes: Trade values are market-price estimates (MWh x hub price), not Powerex/BC Hydro settlements.
The BC-US tie uses one Mid-C price per day, so hour-to-hour timing inside an event is only meaningful on the BC-Alberta tie.
BC load is posted by BC Hydro each business day for the previous day(s); until then load shows as pending.
Load % of peak uses the highest hourly load in the 365 days before the event day.
